Definition: from G4862 and G4155; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd:--choke, throng.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus explains that the seed among the thorns is the one who hears the word, and the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, so he becomes unfruitful. Luke adds pleasures of this life to the list, and the choking is slow: the word is not stolen at once, it is crowded out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe riches and pleasures can choke the word without ever denying it, and I hold that I must keep the ground clear around what God has planted in me.
